cards.hint: Recall balanced forces with no net push
options: the thrust is equal to the drag
the thrust is greater than the drag
the lift is greater than the weight
cards.quote: an airplane can maintain a constant speed and level flight, in which the lift is equal to the weight, and the thrust is equal to the drag.
cards.stem: In level flight at constant speed, which propulsion balance is maintained

cards.hint: Think about steady wind and steady motion over ground
options: The ground speed remains constant
The wind speed keeps changing rapidly
The lift keeps decreasing to zero
cards.quote: The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.
cards.stem: When wind speed stays steady, what stays steady for a cruising aircraft

cards.hint: Think about speed held over the longest time aloft
options: ground speed times the maximum time
fuel load minus the cruise weight
takeoff speed plus landing distance
cards.quote: The maximum distance that the aircraft can fly is then equal to the ground speed times the maximum time (tmax).
cards.stem: What determines the farthest distance an aircraft can fly on its fuel load

cards.hint: Think about needing to return to base
options: half of the range as specified here
twice the one way mission distance
full range for a one way trip
cards.quote: The combat radius would be half of the range as specified here.
cards.stem: For a round trip military mission, what does combat radius mean
